methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); electric utility signals on FPL Group's own lines

pit_profile.why: NextEra Energy, Inc.: 'FPL is a rate-regulated electric utility engaged primarily in the generation, transmission, distribution and sale of electric energy in Florida.' and 'NEER produces the majority of its electricity from clean and renewable sources, including wind, solar and hydro.'; among its risk factors, 'NEE's and FPL's business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects may be adversely affected by the extensive regulation of their business.', 'NEE's and FPL's business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects can be materially adversely affected by weather conditions, including, but not limited to, the impact of severe weather.' and 'NEE's and FPL's business could be negatively affected by federal or state laws or regulations mandating new or additional limits on the production of greenhouse gas emissions.' (its own FY2011 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an electric utility on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on climate change stay here (the PEP obesity rule)

classification.quality_note: NextEra Energy, Inc.: 'FPL is a rate-regulated electric utility engaged primarily in the generation, transmission, distribution and sale of electric energy in Florida.' and 'NEER produces the majority of its electricity from clean and renewable sources, including wind, solar and hydro.'; among its risk factors, 'NEE's and FPL's business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects may be adversely affected by the extensive regulation of their business.', 'NEE's and FPL's business, financial condition, results of operations and prospects can be materially adversely affected by weather conditions, including, but not limited to, the impact of severe weather.' and 'NEE's and FPL's business could be negatively affected by federal or state laws or regulations mandating new or additional limits on the production of greenhouse gas emissions.' (its own FY2011 10-K); no disruption theme in the registry is live for an electric utility on this date, so the watch list is empty and the 10-K's words on climate change stay here (the PEP obesity rule). durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; Ratio B 1.38x; +38% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.24; conservative 2yr -7%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -5.6%/yr (worst year FY02-FY11, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +-14.4%/yr (Q3 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +9.5%/yr (FY02-FY11 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +18.2%/yr (best 2-yr run FY02-FY11); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: NEE (retrospective, 2012-10-25) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.38x (34.0% downside to Bear $46 / +24.7% upside to Bull $87) | Adj composite 1.99 vs market 3.23: gap -1.24 [OVERVALUED] | +38% above the EPP floor $50 (11x FY12E $4.59) | Conservative 2-yr case: -7.4% total (-3.7%/yr) | At 15.2x FY12E the 15% hurdle price $92 sits above the BULL case; FPL energy sales -2.8% in Q3 2012, forward revenues -12.3% (no Q4 2012 revenue guide, Q3 2012 revenue as reported); no disruption theme is live for an electric utility on this date.
